provenance: Codex (gpt-6-astra) started this patch and stopped at its usage limit; its intermediate D1 failures were sandbox listen EPERM only. A Claude Opus 5.5 session outside that sandbox re-ran Codex's tree unchanged, audited it, fixed further findings test-first and produced every count below.
design_implemented: Browser URL is exactly /pair/claim (no query, fragment or path credential); legacy token URLs/POSTs rejected without reflection; installer accepts no other claim URL and prints only the credential-free URL.

Three separate random values, SHA-256 hashes only at rest: 256-bit polling token (installer memory, 10 min); 128-bit browser code (local macOS dialog over stdin with never-share warning, 5 min, one-time); 256-bit confirmation value bound to verified issuer+subject+email, session device/key and files-v1 scope (max 5 min).

Two same-origin, Access-verified POSTs: code review, then explicit file-access confirmation; caller device/owner/key fields, email-only identity, account switch, replay and widened scope rejected without rows.
Every claim-batch write rechecks reviewed identity/device/key/scope/expiry; explicit NOT EXISTS guards replace INSERT OR IGNORE so any constraint failure rolls back the whole claim.

No two live pending sessions per Mac identity or agent key; lost start response retry returns 409 until expiry; installer never rotates identity and records completion only after signed device verification.
pair/status reports cancelled when the bound identity, user or device is inactive; every /mcp request re-resolves identity -> active user -> exactly one active device.
Malformed MCP_AUTH_MODE / ACCESS_DEVICE_ROUTING (empty, non-string, unknown) -> 503 before registry access, never the personal Mac; unset MCP_AUTH_MODE keeps static mode.

Claim pages: no-store, no-referrer, nosniff, X-Frame-Options DENY, COOP same-origin, CSP default-src 'none' with form-action 'self', frame-ancestors 'none', base-uri 'none'; no script or external resource.
Migration 0007 additive with CHECKs: 64-hex credential hashes, consent_scope only files-v1, integer consent times.

residual_risks: Device-code phishing: whoever enters a shown code first (with an Access-admitted identity) binds that account to the Mac; the Mac cannot yet display which account claimed it; dialog cancel does not cancel the server session (no Mac-side cancel endpoint).
Strict one-time code/confirmation: double submit or a lost review response consumes the code; re-run after the 10-minute session.
Review page holds the account-bound confirmation value in a hidden field; useless to other identities, but no-store does not prove browser erasure.
Installer recovery confirms via signed device status, which does not reflect identity revocation (MCP still denies).
Example BETA_ENROLL_RATE (5/min per address) vs 3-4 enroll-class requests per pairing must be checked in staging.
Real Access login/expiry redirects, browser history/back/resubmission and deployed logging remain staging observations.
